utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-5/18-PT, the Prosecutor versus Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone. Mr. Karadzic, can you confirm to me, first of all, again that you continue to represent yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I now have appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Alan Tieger; Ann Sutherland; and case manager, Iain Reid, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Since the last Status Conference and the intimation of pleas on behalf of the accused following the amendment of the indictment, there has been ongoing Chambers business in relation to a large number of issues in the case and there has been one Rule 65 ter meeting at which all three Judges of the Pre-Trial Chamber presided. Certain matters discussed at that meeting will be the subject of further discussion and possibly decision in the course of this meeting -- this hearing today. The first item that I would like to deal with, Mr. Karadzic, is the question of your -- what you describe as your legal team. Because it may be that a discussion here this afternoon would be beneficial in clarifying possible misunderstandings about what is available to you and how to go about ensuring that what is available is in fact made available. And for that reason I've asked that a member of the Registry from OLAD should be present, and Mr. Ambach is in court. You will recollect that a decision was made about the way in which Rule 68 material is disclosed to you, and you have made an application for certification to appeal that decision. However, you will also recollect that part of the decision encouraged both you and OLAD to discuss further the arrangements for access to the electronic disclosure system. I understood that following that decision efforts would be made by both you and OLAD to try to resolve this, but I also understand now that you may not have made any further application for additional staff to have access to the electronic disclosure system. Now, can you explain to me your position on that, what steps you intend to take to try to improve the availability of access.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, My Lord, for putting this item on the agenda. I had intended to raise the issue as well. I received your decision, and I indeed do wish to appeal that decision. But in the meantime I had sent a request to the Registry for access for three legal interns assisting my legal team to have access to electronic -- access to the electronic disclosure system. Today I was supposed to find out whether they would be working pro bono, they have been working pro bono throughout, but I don't know whether they will -- their expenses will be covered. I received that only today. The mailmen really like me a lot. Just before this Status Conference, or rather, before each and every Status Conference we have I get loads of material from the OTP and from the Registry, and I really cannot look at all the things that we're supposed to deal with at these Status Conferences. I will appeal if I'm given certification to do so, but in the meantime I would like a larger number of the members of my team to have access to electronic disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What I'm now going to do is ask Mr. Ambach if he will explain to us what the understanding of OLAD is as to the application you've made and to explain to us also what decision, if any, has been made on any application you have made. Please listen carefully to what he says because I do believe there is some misunderstanding in the communications occurring here, and it's important that rather than have written communications passing back and forward to no good purpose that we get this resolved if possible today. Now, Mr. Ambach, can you assist us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have indeed received a request of the 16th of March from the accused; however, this request is confusing to the Registry to an extent in that the accused requested the designation of current legal interns as members of his Defence team. It is the position of OLAD, of the Registry, that it does not assign any pro bono associates to the accused. The Registry merely notes the fact that the accused has retained a pro bono legal associate. Now, with regard to the request of the 16th of March, it was not and it is not clear to the Registry whether the accused seeks the assignment of the persons named in the request pursuant to the remuneration scheme or whether it -- whether the accused rather seeks the acknowledgement of the above Defence team members as pro bono legal associates. I hope that this clarifies to an extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many persons were involved, Mr. Ambach, in this application?

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused requested the assignment of three persons who are currently serving as legal interns of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, there are two issues here. There's the question of whether someone is assigned to you as a legal associate which has the effect that that person is remunerated to some extent; and separately, there is the question of whether anyone, whether remunerated or not, has access to confidential material and therefore is authorised to have unrestricted access to the electronic disclosure system. Now, when you made this application, was it directed to the question of assignment so that they would receive payment, or was it directed to the question of allowing them to access the electronic disclosure system?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for my entire team consisting of eight persons who are supposed to assist me and to be remunerated by the Registry, well, I haven't set up that team yet. There's only three so far, one is a researcher and two are legal associates. They can stay here only three days a month. That is to say that I have no possibility whatsoever of preparing an effective defence and of making sure on my part that these proceedings are fair and proper. I am asking for these associates to be approved one by one because I cannot make the request for all eight at the same time because I want them to deal with different fields, say civil law, et cetera. So I would want to have them all approved one by one so I know what fields I have approved as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I want to interrupt you because I don't think you're addressing the question I asked you. The question is: When you made this application relating to three people, was that for them to be assigned as part of your team so that they get paid, or was it so that they would have access to the electronic disclosure system? Please address that question, then we'll turn to any wider issues that arrive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The latter. On the basis of your decision I asked that documents be submitted to me only with the numbers marked in keeping with Rule 65. I asked for these three persons who have already been working pro bono to have access to the electronic system so that they could have these documents submitted to me. If you allow me, I also wanted to say that I'm pleased actually that you want to establish how the defence preparations are getting along because they are not really getting along very well at all as if there were some omissions on my part, whereas the case is different. It seems that somebody else is trying to prove that I cannot represent myself. I can represent myself but if no obstacles are placed in my path.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ambach, considering what's just been said, that this was meant to be an application for access to the electronic disclosure system -- I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but it may be timely. I just wanted to note that I was advised shortly before coming into court this afternoon that OTP had been contacted about access to the EDS system for three of Mr. Karadzic's associates. I just wanted to let the Court know because it seems part of the ongoing discussion and ongoing process, and we indicated no objection and would do whatever -- would fulfil whatever part of the process is within our province.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Now, Mr. Ambach, can you now tell us what the communication sent by OLAD in response to this application was.

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, the Registry asked the accused specifically to clarify upon the question of whether the assignment of a legal associate or of legal associates was requested or whether it was rather meant as a notification that the persons named in his request would be retained from now on as pro bono legal associates connected, with request that these persons be granted access to EDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that the communication that he would receive today?

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: That is exactly the communication that he received today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, you've had the answer to that, which is it's the latter. In light of that, do you require any further information about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The Registry is of course grateful to the accused if he provides the Registry with the curriculum vitae of the persons that the accused has decided to retain as his pro bono legal associates; however, there are no further requirements on the side of the Registry when it comes to the Registry noting the fact that the accused has retained pro bono legal associates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ambach, will the decision on access be made without receiving the CDs -- the CVs, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And can we, therefore, invite you to make a more or less immediate decision, in other words, within the next 24 hours, please, on this application so that the matter can be resolved as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karadzic, so far as your application for certification to appeal the decision that we've had some discussion about just now and which has led in fact to this application which I expect is likely to be successful and successful fairly quickly, but the decision is not in our hands and it will be intimated to you by the Registry tomorrow. But in light of all the circumstances and our earlier consideration of your application, the Chamber has decided to refuse you certification to appeal that decision. The issue is whether the combination of the means by which the Prosecution disclose exculpatory material to the accused and the facilities available to him to gain access to the material has resulted in a failure by the Prosecution to implement its disclosure obligation under Rule 68. Since that issue, particularly the question of the facilities for access, is the subject of ongoing consideration by the Registrar, neither leg of the test for certification is met. Even if the test was met, the Chamber would exercise its discretion to refuse to certify the proposed appeal. If you're dissatisfied with the final determination of the Registrar, you can raise the matter before the Chamber afresh, but then you would be raising it on the basis of the facts prevailing at that stage. Now I would like you to raise any other matters you wish to raise in connection with your -- the establishment of your legal team so that we can make sure that anything that's outstanding is dealt with quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wished to say that I have given up on my request to have all material disclosed to me in hard copy, on paper. I've agreed to electronic disclosure. I have a room full of CDs and I'm sort of dealing with it, but this is an additional impediment. In view of this vast amount of material and also the magnitude of these proceedings, this is going to be a far greater trial than any other trial before it. I asked to have a certain number of experts allocated to me and that they be paid not like supplementary staff but in accordance with the seriousness of the work that they do. I'm not asking for any kind of advantage because I represent myself. However, I do not want to have additional obstacles placed in my path because I'm representing myself. If they were to be paid like normal lawyers are paid, then I could give them assignments as to what all the things are that they're supposed to do for me. My investigators even have to say what they are discussing with potential witnesses. Their travel expenses are not paid for. My top-notch experts, my advisors, can be here only three days a month, and finally it's only two of them plus an investigator that have been appointed out of the possible eight. I'm waiting to deal with all of this one by one. You have a motion in respect of one of them, Mr. Sladojevic who was indispensable for me, he lives here, he speaks the Dutch language, so it will be easier for him to prepare for this. I assure you that the proceedings have already taken a very risky path, and it is not very regular either. When am I going to deal with all of this material? You should have been at the 65 ter meeting and hear the OTP how they complained that they do not have enough resources, et cetera, et cetera. And can you imagine what it's like for me? I have to deal with this same material that they have been compiling and presenting. I have to study it here; I have to defend myself here. So there is this inequality of arms, and it is such -- and the disproportion is so vast that regularity as such is brought into question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you've now explained, as you have done before, what you see as an unfair element in the system. What you fail to reflect in what you've said is that there is a perfectly inadequate system of legal aid for full representation for you which you have chosen not to take advantage of, and that of course is aimed at giving you equality of arms with the Prosecution. What you have chosen to do is represent yourself because you claim you can do that. And you are being given what is exceptional in legal systems throughout the world, and that is additional facilities at the expense of this Tribunal to assist you in your venture to represent yourself. Now, quite rightly, you identify that there are limitations on that, and these limitations are recognised and have been there for some time throughout your period here. You have outstanding an appeal against the Chamber's decision in relation to this issue, and I can appreciate your frustration at the time that legal proceedings tend to take. But at the same time, you must recognise your obligation to prepare for the possibility that your appeal will be unsuccessful. And it is, I think, surprising to us that you have not made any further applications other than for Mr. Sladojevic to be assigned in this way. And unless you make applications, then it won't be possible for the Registry to deal with any. You tell us that we can expect another four applications on top of him, but these have not yet arrived. What is the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment when I see what I have at my disposal, I will decide who the other four are going to be. I cannot make up my team with just minor players. I have all the best players. I have to see what's been approved in order to see how I'm going to go next. I'm not asking for any concessions. The fact that I'm representing myself and I'm not a lawyer is a handicap, but I don't want to have any other handicaps. I've seen here how people defended themselves as objects of the trials, and I'm not going to allow that. The truth cannot be heard if somebody who was there and who knows everything does not represent it before the Trial Chamber. I cannot accept any other representation but my own. I have to represent myself. I have to have a team, and I have to have the equality of arms. I have to have the same thing as the Prosecution does, vast funds and everything else. Later on I will tell you what the Prosecution is currently doing in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and at this moment I cannot even dream of attempting to do any such thing. That's why it is indispensable for me to have the appointment of those who I have applied for. When I see what has been approved and when I see what is still missing, then I will make my decision on the other four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You have made reference there to not wanting to be considered an object of the proceedings, and that reference I understand. I understand why you might feel yourself to be in that position. But I think I would be failing in my duty, you having raised the matter, if I were not to point out to you that throughout your time here this Bench has expressed its willingness to consider a situation in which albeit you are represented by counsel, you yourself are also permitted to play an active part in your own defence. The Bench has expressed throughout its willingness to be flexible in the arrangements it makes for the conduct of your trial, and you have steadfastly refused to consider that. Now, that is your privilege, and I don't criticise you for it. I simply intend to ensure that the whole story is portrayed in any discussion we have on this subject. It's also important not to ignore the fact that you have had a significant number of pro bono legally qualified personnel providing assistance to you to the point that the submissions made by you have been many; they have been helpful; they have been instructive. So the picture that the Chamber has is one of an accused person at the moment doing a pretty good job of representing himself on legal challenges. However, we remain conscious of the size of the case, the volume of material, the difficulty for an individual in that situation to prepare adequately and conduct his own defence. But you know also that the Trial Chamber recognises that there are disadvantages, too, that go with self-representation. And that road having been chosen, then there may be certain difficulties that we all have to address as best we can as we proceed through the trial. Now, it seems, Mr. Karadzic, that there's no more we can do at this stage today on the question of the composition of your legal team, but we will be prepared to return to that issue at any future Status Conference should you consider it appropriate to raise it again. And what I'd like to move to now is a very specific issue again and that is the preliminary motion challenging the jurisdiction of the Tribunal on the basis of the agreement you say that you had from a representative of the United States, Mr. Holbrooke, that you would not be prosecuted. The Chamber is quite happy to suspend the running of any time-limit for that motion until the appeal that relates to it which has been outstanding for some time is determined. And therefore, we will issue an order in writing at the appropriate stage when we are in a position to do so about the time you have to submit such a motion. Can I take it that what you intend to do is withdraw the initial motion that you made when you were first detained and appeared here and to submit an entirely fresh motion, focusing the issue on the basis of the situation as it can now be presented?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Just briefly I would like to respond to your first question. I'm very grateful to you for taking this into account, and I would like to ask you to take under advisement that I will always represent myself. You mentioning the possibility that this might change only encourages the Registry and gives them a false hope that I will accept counsel. That will not happen. You are right, I am going to withdraw my August 2008 motion and replace it by a new one when my investigators complete the investigations. You have -- may have seen in your times that we have received very convincing data about new witnesses in the state department in the United States and elsewhere, and when that investigation is over a new motion will be filed which will be much more precise. When I say "Holbrooke," I can imply that he represented the United States, but there is also proof that he acted on behalf of the entire international community, and the evidence to that effect cannot be challenged. And I'm very grateful to you with regard to the running of the time-limit. I also would like to thank all the professors and interns who are assisting me in providing you with a clear picture of the legal aspects of the proceedings so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you're right that your challenge can be characterised on the basis that it was an agreement that you claim was made on behalf of more than the United States, but just how specific that can be stated remains to be seen if it is of course relevant at all. What we will do is consider what we should do in relation to the existing motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying the position, Mr. Karadzic. We will regard the motion of the 6th of August now as withdrawn, and we will suspend meanwhile the running of the time-limit for submitting a jurisdictional challenge based on the Holbrooke agreement, and we will issue in due course a further order specifying when that jurisdictional challenge has to be submitted to us. I want to turn now to the Prosecution on the question of disclosure, and the disclosure I have in mind initially is that in terms of Rule 66(A)(ii), which is the disclosure of statements of proposed witnesses for the trial. Now, Mr. Tieger, one of the things that will be done following today's meeting is the establishment and publication to the parties of a work-plan for the remainder of the pre-trial phase of this case. And into that work-plan we intend to insert a date for disclosure in terms of Rule 66(A)(ii) and may even be able to make an order this afternoon. Can you tell me the state of preparedness for full disclosure of these statements at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't relate more I think than was discussed at the 65 ter Conference. I appreciate the fact that this is an opportunity to make that information generally public. I think as the Court is aware, the categories of witnesses have been broken down to some extent in terms of internationals, crime base, et cetera. The disclosure of the internationals as related at the 65 ter Conference is basically complete. I think the Court was also made aware that with respect to the additional witnesses, including the large number of crime base witnesses, that remains to be done for the most part and that hasn't changed to an appreciable extent since the 65 ter Conference. I don't know if the Court is asking for some specific additional information beyond that, but I assume that my response generally covers the Court's inquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If we were to specify the 30th April for disclosure of statements, would that present a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, it would -- I would ask for an additional week I think, but I -- I'm not -- I mean, I don't feel I'm in a position to resist the Court on that. Obviously, if that order was made we would bend every effort toward fulfilling it and would expect to do so. Based on my discussions, I think the additional week would represent a somewhat more realistic dead-line for the personnel involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, what I'm asking about is the disclosure to you of all the statements of witnesses that the Prosecution intend to lead. The Chamber had in mind prior to coming on to the Bench today the end of April as a date by which that we should order disclosure of these to you. The Prosecution ask for another week beyond that. Do you have any comment to make?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By the magnitude and the number of witnesses, this is going to be a huge process. The Prosecution have announced 26 expert witnesses, for them I have not received satisfactory material. And this also refers to your decision about my knowledge of English. I can control what I speak because I chose the English vocabulary. But what others are saying what I'm supposed to read that was written by others, I can't control this. So your impression that my English is good is deceptive. I have to employ five to ten interpreters and translators and ask for the Registry -- for the translations to be paid. This is another problem with expert witnesses and their testimonies and statements in the previous cases. The second thing that is not acceptable on my part when it comes to expert witnesses is that I have to pick and choose from various reports and various testimonies they've provided so far and find things that may be relative to myself. This is an additional effort on my part. I suggest that the Prosecutor should be ordered to submit consolidated expert reports in the form that would be specifically relative to myself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I will come to the expert reports. I'm looking generally at - I should have made it clear - statements of other witnesses. The experts fall under a different rule, and we'll come to them specifically in the course of the discussion. So far as the other witnesses are concerned, and you've heard them described as falling into various categories, but the two mentioned were international witnesses and those who are witnesses to the actual commission of the crimes that you are alleged to be responsible for, it's the disclosure of these statements, and the suggested date is about the 7th of May. Now, do you have anything to say on that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I've been informed that 80 out of over 400 witnesses as crime-base witnesses have been disclosed, but I've never been told which witnesses are those. I've received hundred and thousands of pages. Now I have to guess which witnesses have actually been disclosed. I'm asked to be provided a specification as to which of those witnesses, and I have not received any disclosure for the remainder of the witnesses. I will need a lot of time, a lot of resources to deal with that vast material. I have to investigate the witnesses, the events that they are testifying about. So you can only imagine how difficult this is going to be. I'm asking for this to happen as soon as possible, and then I'm asking for sufficient time to be able to study all those statements. You saw at the 65 ter Conference that the representative of the OTP even mentioned Croatia as the crime place -- base. Please, this is the first time I hear that I should be tried for something that was happening in Croatia. This is incredible. After eight months having been in detention I hear this for the first time. When is it that I'm finally going to hear what is it that I'm being charged with without any extensions, without making this monstrous proceedings even bigger and even lengthier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No doubt I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, but I think the mention of Croatia was to explain to you that the parts of a report that related to Croatia would not be part of the case against you. There are two items arising from what you've said that I will seek to clarify. The first is your reference to interpreters or translators. I know that the facility is available to you to have language assistants if you wish to make use of it. Are you saying that you have already sought to have an interpretation facility?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In keeping with your previous decision, I expected to be submitted testimonies and transcripts that are relative to me in the Serbian language. And in that case I would not have asked for interpreters and translators. Since you have changed the decision, I have to do what the OTP should have done. I have to employ people to translate things for me or to transcribe things from the audio tapes. I have already seen major mistakes and changes when it comes, for example, to Mladic's request for people to be disarmed and it has been translated as Mladic's request for them to surrender. These are major discrepancies. I should not be dealing with English statements made on the part of other people. If I am certified to appeal that, I will appeal this because it would be much easier for the OTP to order for the transcription to be made from the Serbian original than for me to decide the essence of the translated sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I be clear on this. The mistake that you've referred to just now, is that in the translation from Serbian to English, or from English to Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a translation from Serbian into English. This is the translation of an intercept or a document where Mladic is quoted as telling them that they have to disarm, whereas it should have been for them to surrender, and these are two completely different things. The meaning should have been that they should throw their weapons and leave the area, disarm themselves and leave the area. That was the meaning of Mladic's words, and this has been misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Of course that particular problem which is an example of the sort of problem that can occasionally arise in an environment where language has to be translated, that has nothing to do with the question of whether things should be translated into Serbian as you, I'm sure, appreciate. Now, can I ask Mr. Tieger to clarify one thing. Mr. Karadzic makes a point that a lot of statements have already been disclosed, but the actual witness list may relate to only a limited number of these and he may not be aware of which. Is that the position, that he will not at this stage know which of the crime-base statements disclosed are going to be or do relate to the witnesses who will give evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The -- well, let me -- I see Ms. Sutherland is about to perhaps elucidate this further. My understanding is -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly open to any kind of clarification of this issue, but it seems to me there really is not much room for that kind of problem to arise for the following reasons. Number one, with respect - let me focus on the crime-base witnesses for a moment - we will be disclosing them pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii) and indicating as such, meaning they are persons intended to be called as witnesses, so they will be specifically identified as such in the nature of the disclosure. Number two, my understanding is that the index that accompanies the materials bears the identification or name of the witness, so that kind of comparison could be made if there was some sort of confusion about whether or not the witness was intended to be on the list. And finally, I believe that it -- to the extent that a witness's statement might be disclosed pursuant to Rule 68, that would be disclosed on EDS. And I think the witness statements intended to be disclosed under Rule 66(A)(ii) as witness statements are disclosed on CD. So I think there are a number of safe-guards that would prevent that kind of confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, I understand that. I think the accused's position was there's 80 of them, as he understands it, already disclosed but not perhaps formally under 66(A)(ii), but effectively disclosed because you've been going through an ongoing disclosure process. And up until now it would not be possible for him to identify which of the many witness statements relate to people who will actually give evidence in court. I appreciate you will clarify it. All I wanted to know was whether at this point in time it's impossible for him to tell which statements that he has already received in one form or another relate to people who will actually be witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With respect to the crime base, I believe that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the Chamber is minded to grant your application for disclosure by the -- a week after the 30th. I don't know what day of the week the 7th of May is, but whatever the appropriate date is around that time. But if you hold off until then identifying who the witnesses actually are, then there's nothing the accused can do meanwhile with the material which has already been disclosed, as I say, in one form or another. So what we were going to do was ask you whether you could provide that additional information as soon as possible so that the -- so that the material which is disclosed already can be utilised. I'm conscious of the fact that the order for your 65 ter list might even be later, although that remains to be determined. So all I'm looking for is the application of some common sense in the disclosure process so that it's not all lumped on the accused on the last day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I understood the Court's request in that light, and I think there was an indication already at the 65 ter Conference that we intended to disclose seriatim rather than wait for the final dead-line and disclose them all in one lump. So that would certainly be the case. I don't know that -- I guess I can check to see whether any disclosure has been made to date of witnesses intended to be on the list or who -- who we will determine during the course of the upcoming period should be on the list, and therefore advise the accused as soon as possible that he already has that material. But I understand the Court's concern which is to get -- as soon as we have the information to get the information to the accused as soon as we can, rather than wait for an upcoming dead-line to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it's reasonable to make the observation at this stage, the general observation, that in dealing with a case involving a self-represented accused, the Court behaves differently from the way in which it would behave in relation to a case where a counsel appears. And I think the Prosecution has to do the same and, in a sense, provide assistance to the accused above and beyond what would be done in the case of a represented accused. And the reason for that is purely practical, that the system in general will function less efficiently and, indeed, could inhibit a fair and expeditious trial if exceptional arrangements were not taken in a situation like this. So we're asking that you do your utmost to stagger the presentation of material so that it's coming as soon as possible and identify as clearly as possible what that material relates to in his case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, it means -- that means that we can, I think, consider what order to make now in relation to Rule 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we will grant the -- or appoint the date suggested by the Prosecution, that is, the 7th of May, for disclosure of all statements of all witnesses other than experts, which we'll deal with separately. Mr. Ambach, we don't really need to detain you, I think, any longer. If anything arises that requires assistance from your department, then we'll contact you, but you're now free to leave, and we're extremely grateful to you for being here and assisting us this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. AMBACH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I now want to deal with expert witnesses. And, Mr. Karadzic, you have some submissions to make, so it might be as well if we hear from you first of all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that I'm not intimidated by this number of 26 experts, expert witnesses that is. But I shall state my views on that when my own experts study all the material, all the documentation, that is to say the CVs of these expert witnesses and also their findings. This is truly work for experts, so my own attitude will be based on the positions taken by my own experts once they've studied the entire material involved. What is very important for me is that I am faced with this ocean of material, and I have to deal with bits and pieces that I have to pick and choose. There is nothing consolidated, nothing that I am specifically charged with. It would have been a lot easier in that case; this way it's going to take a lot longer because I will probably call the same number of witnesses, and I will ask for their work to be paid, both in terms of analysis and in preparing my defence and for actually testifying for my defence. So it is important to receive consolidated material that pertains to me specifically so that I do not have to guess what has to do with me. As for language and translation, once again, please take this seriously. I kindly ask you to do that. I'm not asking for anything special. Your Excellency, you put it right, translation can be a problem, but the OTP can transcribe Serbo-Croatian audio material. With all due respect for Your Excellencies and your respective countries, but please look at what the situation is. NATO waged war against us; NATO arrested me; NATO wanted to do other bad, serious things against me. All three of your countries are NATO members, and now I even have to deal with the language of the NATO countries. I have to defend myself in a NATO-country language. There are many elements, therefore, indicating that this trial cannot be fair from any point of view. I'm trying to make things look better than they actually do, and of course I'm trying to help myself as well in the process. However, I'm going to state my views on the experts once I've received all the material, hopefully translated into the Serbian language, and their testimony too. Then I would like my own experts to have some time to study this material, and then they will advise me, and then I will take my position as to what I feel the expertise of the 26 experts is like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that was divided into two parts, Mr. Karadzic. You've obviously got something off your chest, and perhaps that's just as well. But you can take it from me here and now that your submissions in this Court will be confined to what is relevant to what we have to consider and decide. Now please bear that in mind, and don't let's have any issues that go to the personal involvement of a Bench which is properly constituted consisting of Judges who come here on a totally impartial basis to do the job that's been assigned to them by the United Nations. Let that be an end of the political grand-standing, and let us concentrate on the issues in the trial. And there you do have a point, because this is a very large number of experts to be handled. But it would be irresponsible, I would suggest to you, just to draw down the blinds and say, I'm going to do nothing about this until my experts have studied the matter. Because these experts fall into a very large number of different categories, and some of them on reflection may turn out to be not very controversial. Now, are you indicating that you're not prepared to look at the material relating to expert evidence objectively to see if in fact it is in dispute? Does it in the end of the day matter whether at the top of an autopsy report about someone who undoubtedly is very dead the name "Radovan Karadzic" appears? Plainly, it doesn't matter. So what we would ask you to do is bring common sense to bear on this issue and try to identify the expert material that really needs to be challenged. And that may be most of these reports in the end of the day, but I doubt very much if it's all of them. Now, is your position that no matter what time you are allocated to consider these reports at this stage won't matter, you'll just take a broad approach and challenge every one on every possible basis?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Most probably I am not going to oppose any one of these experts appearing. However, I think that I am going to challenge their findings in their entirety or in part, and I'll do that on the basis of the knowledge and advice provided by my experts and my advisors. As for credibility, as for competence, as for eligibility, I'll leave that for the courtroom; however, I have to say that I'm not concerned nor intimidated by the number of these experts, except that I will have to have an equal number of experts. Of course I will be dealing with this, but I won't be able to give my final word on the basis of that. As for my final word on the experts and their findings, it is indispensable for my experts to give me advice as to what I'm supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Our concern, though, has to be at the moment with following the Rules, and these Rules allow you to do two things in relation to expert evidence. You can either accept it or cross-examine -- seek to cross-examine the witness, that's number one; and the second thing is you can challenge the qualifications of the witness as an expert or the relevance of the statement or report of the witness. Now, the normal rule would give you 30 days in which to decide your position, that's 30 days from the time at which the report is formally disclosed to you, and the Prosecution have been going through the exercise of formally disclosing these by filing a notice to that effect. What I'm trying to establish is whether 30 days is the right period of time to allow you to take your stand, to indicate to us what your position will be in relation to these experts. Now, do you have any comment on that, whether the passage of time will make any difference to the position you will take at this stage, the pre-trial stage, of the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that is the time given to me to present my stand or my position, I think that will be sufficient for just presenting my position; however, after that I hope that I will have enough time to respond. Just taking a stand, well, yes, that could be done within the provided time-frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There may be some misunderstanding here. There's no question of you having to respond to an expert's statement. The issues for you to address are set out in Rule 94 bis(B), and within 30 days of the filing of the notice which has been occurring in relation to each of these experts, you have to say whether you want the witness to attend for cross-examination and also say whether you challenge the qualifications of the expert of the relevance of the report. That's all you have to do at this stage. As far as responding is concerned, your own experts will in due course give whatever evidence you seek to lead from them, but that's well down the line, as you know, that's a long way away. So even though it is a long way away, it's, I think, unrealistic not to try to assess which of these ought really to be the subject of challenge and whether the evidence in the case on issues such as pathology and other related forensic issues is genuinely in dispute or whether we can find a way of dealing with that without spending valuable time in court on it. The danger of paying attention in court to unnecessary cross-examination of witnesses is that it diverts attention from the really crucial issues in the case, and the parties themselves may not effectively present their case properly if they get diverted into issues which are immaterial. So we remain hopeful that you will see in some of these reports material that you don't really want to challenge, that you can accept, and try to concentrate on the ones which you plainly -- I can see now some that you're plainly going to want to challenge. So what we'll do is simply note that no order is being made in relation to the operation of Rule 94 bis, which means that your time-limit for filing your notice in relation to each of the experts is 30 days from the date on which the Prosecution filed their notice. I now turn to the Prosecution to clarify when this process will be completed. At the 65 ter Conference the position was a bit unsatisfactory, and I hope that the situation may have changed a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it did change a bit, but I suspect with regard to the -- what I consider to be the one -- well, the relative handful of problematic prospective disclosures, I'm not sure the situation has changed. It -- I understood -- I mean, there are a number of disclosures, and I can go through them one by one, but I think the Court was made aware of those during the course of the 65 ter Conference. The bulk of the disclosures will be made on or before the end of this month. There were, as I mentioned, a handful that I understood and that were related to the Court as being anticipated for May, one in particular that was anticipated for the end of May that the Court expressed concern about. My first question therefore would be: Does the Court wish me to go through these individually or address myself to the disclosures that are anticipated for May?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the one that was for the end of May was Mark Thompson, but I understood that was changed to the end of April by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what was the other one for the end of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh yeah, sorry, do we -- is it number 26 on the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The Rule 70 witness. Now, his name can now be disclosed, can it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And there are previous documents -- previous reports done by him and all that was outstanding was some new addendum?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, does that relate to matters on which no other expert will give evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And why is it going to take to the 31st of May to make that available?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That matter has been broached with the expert as I understand it. Certainly more than willing -- first of all, I'm more than willing to again raise the Court's concerns and see if the schedule can be modified in any way. But I can tell the Court that we express our strong interest in the earliest possible completion date. I believe that was understood by Mr. Butler, and I can only relate the nature of his schedule and the nature of the effort involved led him to conclude that he wouldn't be in a position to complete the report before that time. Now, what I can relate by way of some modest consolation in that regard is that we've disclosed the other reports related to Mr. Butler. This will be supplemental information. I think that it would be relatively -- and I obviously use the term guardedly, and then easy to absorb in the wake of an understanding of and a necessary review of the other reports upon which the Prosecution relies which were prepared by Mr. Butler previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One other matter that Mr. Karadzic has raised and which the Trial Chamber raised at the 65 ter Conference was the use of reports which relate to other accused and from which parts may have to be redacted for the purpose of this or at least ignored for the purpose of this case. And following on that, in one instance at least, there was notification of a change of position and that Riedlmayer's report would be reviewed and one prepared for the purpose of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, is it going to take time to prepare it, or is that instantly available?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, that will take some time, and that's another matter that would be ready by the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, are there any others where that's being done?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, but no -- no other anticipated reports that are different from what was related at the time of the 65 ter. And what I mean by that is I think the understanding at the time of the 65 ter Conference was that the Prosecution would rely on the previously submitted reports by Mr. Riedlmayer. That has given way to the anticipation of a new -- entirely new report, case-specific report, which will be ready by the end of the month. With the exception of that change, the positions related at the 65 ter with respect to the submission of reports remains the same. Some dates have changed, I should indicate that, and that is the anticipated submission date for the Theunens report, which was the end of the month, and I believe was ended as the end of the month --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- is now the middle of the month, April 15th. And the Phillips report is roughly the same, although a little earlier, anticipated for the 11th of this month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is one for which the date has already passed which I don't think we have. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson's report; correct. And that is anticipated for April 9th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I think the one -- yeah, the other two late -- very late dates were Thompson propaganda, we mentioned it a moment ago. It doesn't seem a subject you would expect to take all this time to write about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say the late date, I mean, you're talking about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's still quite some time. This date has been in this list for some time. That one can't be hurried along?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, as I indicated before, I will be more than happy to recontact Mr. Thompson to see if that's possible, certainly at a minimum to relate the Court's interest in the earliest possible submission date, and we'll do that as quickly as possible. But I believe -- I mean, I hope and I do believe that that interest was conveyed before, and I would expect that the projected date was arrived at with that understanding, that is, the understanding that we hope to get it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, is there anything further you want to say on the dates for submitting the expert reports, bearing in mind now that all the dates proposed are in the month of April with the exception of one -- oh, and one other that needs to be clarified. Sorry, Mr. Tieger, is there a date for number 25?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe there were two others that were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, yes, van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. Torkildsen was raised at the 65 ter. I know that's a matter that Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff has been in contact with the expert on, has -- again, has pushed for the earliest possible date. I don't believe based on the witness's schedule and the amount of material he anticipates reviewing that it would be realistic for me to suggest that further contact with the expert will accelerate the date. I'm not refusing to do so, but I am aware of the efforts that were made previously to move this process forward, and I think the realities of the situation are that that's the -- that that remains a realistic date. With respect to -- I'm trying to use the numbers which are not on this particular list, if you will bear with me a moment. Number 24 General Vegh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff related his particular circumstances at the 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The submission of the report from number 23, Mr. Van der Weijden, that date occurs because, as I understand it, the expert is away from his home, out of his home country, will not be returning until roughly that date, and requires some specific materials in order to complete the process. So it's purely a matter of logistics, unfortunately, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And 25, I don't -- there's no date there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think -- Your Honour, that notice was filed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ah, okay. Yeah. In fact, I have it noted. Sorry, it's my mistake. Now, Mr. Karadzic, is there anything that you would wish to submit in relation to the dates by which these reports should be tendered?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, the sooner the better. I will be in a position to comply with my obligations within the 30-days' dead-line if the Registry provides me with everything that I need. For 26 experts I should take at least one day for each of them and decide what to do with them. That's a very tall order, but I will be able to comply if everything else is in place, if I don't have any problems with nominating my assistants, and if I have the funds for my 26 experts. And in that sense, I believe that we will be able to respond and that you will be satisfied with our response. We are not going to create any further problems. I would like to ask one more thing, if I orally challenge one of the experts or their findings, does that mean that I have exhausted my right to challenge that same expert in the courtroom? If that be the case, then I would like to reserve my right to challenge the expert in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think I follow what you've just said. If you orally challenge the expert -- you mean you want to do it now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Your proposal was for us to leave as little as possible for the courtroom, and rather to submit written submissions within the 30 days and state what I'm going to do with the expert, whether I'm going to challenge that expert or not. My question was this: If I challenge the expert before the trial in a written form, does that mean that I have relinquished my right on challenging that same expert during the process?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I've obviously not made this clear to you. All that you're being required to do under the Rule is state whether you wish to challenge the expert or not, and the actual challenge will take place in the courtroom. You don't need to say at this stage the basis for the challenge or anything of that nature. That doesn't mean to say that it would be wise not to try to limit the challenge the more time you have and the more familiar you are with the material. There may be only certain things you want to challenge, and it would be helpful later before we get to the witness to know whether you have reduced the area that you wish to challenge him on. All that you must declare at this stage is whether you wish to cross-examine him. And you must also declare whether you are challenging his qualifications or the relevance of his statement, and for that you really should say on what basis you challenge the qualifications that the relevance of his statement. That's rather different. You need to give a basis for that challenge. But as far as cross-examining him in court, you just need to state you intention to do so. We will have to have a break at some stage for purposes related to the recording of the proceedings and now seem an appropriate time to have that break, so we will break for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn just now and resume at 5.00. I don't expect that the hearing will last much more than half an hour after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The Chamber will require the Prosecution to file the expert witness statements and reports in accordance with the anticipated dates as now amended. So going quickly through the list - and please correct me if I inaccurately state any of these dates - Brunborg, the 9th of April; Donia, the 15th of April; Hanson, the 9th of April; Philipps, the 11th of April; Tabeau, the 9th of April and the 1st of May, two different reports; Theunens, the 15th of April; Thompson, the 30th of April; Torkildsen, the 7th of May; Treanor, the 30th of April; van der Weijden, the 15th of May; Vegh, the 7th of May; and Butler, the 31st of May. Now, Mr. Tieger, the accused pointed out that the form in which these reports are presented could be a source of difficulty. And the Chamber without having yet had the opportunity of studying any of them in sufficient detail was concerned at the 65 ter Conference that the recycling of previous reports could create potential difficulty. We simply invite the Prosecution to look carefully at any situation where they might be able to improve the presentation in a way that will make it more easily understood by the accused. We note that steps have already been taken in relation to Nielsen to alert him to parts which are not going to be referred to, albeit they are in the report from the past. And as long as the position is clear, then there will be no problem for either him or the Bench. But we are concerned that there may be some where it's rather a complex exercise to identify what relates to Mr. Karadzic's case and what relates only to other cases. So please be alert to ensuring that any such difficulty is resolved before the reports are filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We still await your interim pre-trial brief, but we do have in mind a date for submission of your final brief with a view to triggering other aspects of Rule 65 ter, and the date that we are considering is the 18th of May. Do you see that as a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, obviously not so I can respond with -- immediately to that. I think we anticipated some aspects at or around that time. If the Court could give me just a moment at least to speak with Ms. Sutherland and Mr. Reid, I would appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask for one nuanced version of that, and that would be to stagger the actual disclosure of the 65 ter exhibit list one week later, so that would mean the brief and the list of documents on the 18th but the actual disclosure a week later. Combining all those on the same day is an enormously complex logistical exercise, and I think in the long run this would result in fewer potential complications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do I take it from that that the bulk of exhibits are not yet disclosed in any form?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The bulk I would say no. I mean, a large number of exhibits have been disclosed, but it would be not more than 50 per cent, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, do you wish to make any comment on the date that the Chamber should fix for the Prosecution to file its final trial brief and the list of witnesses and exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that I do not object to the dead-lines being pushed, but not limitlessly. If I were on provisional release, I would not care. I would like the trial to start as soon as possible but still to be given time to prepare. If I remain in detention, they should speed things along; however, I'm not going to object to their request to be given enough time. I also have to say that I may also need more than 30 days to decide about my own attitude towards their experts. I'm not going to be able to deal with one expert a day, and I will not be able to say after such short period what I am going to do with these experts. I'm talking about the 30-day limit according to Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a different position from the one you took earlier. Are you asking us to reconsider the decision we've already made?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that I am not sure that I will have everything at the disposal that I might need. I'm talking about the funds to pay my experts, all the team members appointed, all the 26 experts. These are my reservations that I have regard to the possibilities to prepare my defence. I'm not objecting to the extension of the dead-lines for the OTP, but I am asking for the same allowances to be given to me. The Registry - and I must repeat - is creating further problems for me as a result of the time they're taking with the appointment of my team members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we're continually straying into other territory. I'll try and take things in some sort of logical order. Just give me a moment to clarify one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we are prepared to reconsider the decision we made earlier, and we will grant additional time and specify what that is in a written order following this hearing. It may be along the lines of giving you effectively for the ones which are either already disclosed or about to be something like six weeks to respond, but for the later ones it will probably retain the 30-day dead-line so that the work can be properly programmed. You should bear in mind, though, that in one case at least the 30 days are almost over, that you've had disclosure in the course of March in, I think, three cases, and that time has already been running according to the Rules, but we will extend that as well so that any misunderstanding is removed, and we will do that in the terms of a written order. The matter you last raised in what you've just said was to complain again about the way the Registry's treating your attempts to build your team. Now, we've been over that today already, and it's clear that you have not submitted applications for all the members of the team you want, and you say that that is because you're not in a position yet to judge the situation. Now, that's not the fault of the Registry as I understand it. I thought you were saying that that depended upon the outcome of the appeal, and if you were successful then there might be a different financial arrangement available. I didn't understand it to be a matter of Registry conduct. Now, what is it you're complaining about in the conduct of the Registry?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem lays in the fact that the three that have already been appointed, the two legal advisors, the highest rank, and the investigator are the people that I was waiting for a long time. And in the meantime one of them has been challenged for a long time quite unjustifiably. And then Mr. Sladojevic, who can be of much assistance to me given all the restrictions that I am facing has been turned down for reasons that are not understandable to me because of the conflict of interest. I have filed my appeal against all the decisions, and my problem is this: I can't provide a whole list because I don't know who will be turned down. It may happen that I may not be able to compose my whole team. If they were to deal with my requests promptly, I will be able to file my requests accordingly. It is in my best interests to have a good team and to have it as soon as possible. I know that there have been some personnel changes in the Registry, but that should not have any impact on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My understanding, Mr. Karadzic, is that there are no applications pending before the Registry. They've dealt with everything. And we've dealt with the one for access to the EDS earlier this afternoon. So which application are you saying the Registry are not -- are sitting on at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are no requests pending. I am waiting for the appeal in the case of the appointment of Mr. Sladojevic. That is the pending request. If Mr. Sladojevic is turned down, then I have to file different proposals. I have to ask for new people, and that is the essence of the matter. If Sladojevic, however, is appointed, then I have room to nominate other people; if not, then I have to find another person who is fluent in English, maybe even in Dutch, who will be here all the time, somebody who will fit in Sladojevic's shoes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've already been giving thought to your case in relation to Sladojevic, and it presents certain problems for the Trial Chamber. The decision on assignment is one for the Registry, and there are limited circumstances in which the Trial Chamber can interfere with that decision. But we will deal with it and make a decision very quickly. I hope you'll have that decision next week. We understand why someone like Mr. Sladojevic is a good choice of -- or has a range of qualifications that are particularly appropriate for your case, but his involvement in other cases does present an issue that has to be carefully considered. And we have to address that and the Registry approach to that before we can make a final decision, but we will do it very quickly now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe that his participation in other cases are now over with the sentences having been passed, so that deals with all the possible problems. So this is not just my caprice. I need to have an advisor on a daily basis who will help me, and the Registry's only paying for their stay in The Hague for three days. It's not good enough for my defence to be successful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please understand, though, that there is a difference between the situation where you simply yourself appoint someone and bear full responsibility for that person, including payment, and the situation where a public authority has to give a stamp of approval to that person's role and different considerations apply. But we will have regard to these and, as I say, give you a decision as soon as possible. And that will be quickly, it will be in the course of next week. Now, the final matter, the matter on which we embarked upon this exchange, relates to the time-limit for the pre-trial brief and of course the lists of witnesses. And we note that you do not take objection to the dates proposed by the Prosecution in light of our indication of the 18th of May. So we will order the final pre-trial brief and list of witnesses and list of exhibits to be filed by the Prosecution on or before the 18th of May. And the copies of the exhibits not so far served on you to be served on or before the 25th of May. But again, that will be the subject of the written order which will follow this hearing. That written order will also contain other relevant dates as part of a work-plan setting out the timetable for the remaining aspects of the pre-trial phase of the case. There are a number of motions now before the Trial Chamber for determination. In some we have responses, and in others we do not yet have responses. We are addressing the ones that we can address, and you can expect decisions in these fairly soon. One of the motions that we have a response to now is that in relation to -- is the first motion of the Prosecution in relation to adjudicated facts. Now, Mr. Tieger, the response of the accused is to say that even if the Trial Chamber does decide to take judicial notice of adjudicated facts, he will nevertheless bring evidence to rebut these. Now, in light of that statement, is the Prosecution likely to simply tender the evidence in any event even if the Trial Chamber does decide to take notice of the adjudicated facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say - and I seek a bit of clarification on the question, Your Honour - when you say "tender the evidence," do you mean in addition to the -- should the Trial Chamber rule favourable on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- motion or adjudicated facts -- with the -- in light of the circumstances you just outlined, would the Prosecution then produce the witnesses in any event?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, because on the basis that these are simply presumptions and not established facts at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would say that depends -- well, first of all, I -- the -- we would not act in disregard of the fact that the motion for adjudicated facts had been ruled on favourably, so it would play a role in our determination of the witnesses to be called. The -- and the determination of whether or not witnesses would have to be called at all with respect to the particular areas addressed by the adjudicated facts would depend, I would think, on some foreshadowing of whether or not the Prosecution would be allowed leeway in rebuttal to address issues raised by the accused and by the Defence in response to the adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One way then of focusing this issue is for you in the pre-trial brief to mention the adjudicated facts and their place in your scheme of the case which might lead to the Trial Chamber requiring -- in fact, the Rules would then require the accused in his pre-trial brief to specify those with which he takes issue. But you'll understand our concern that a great deal of time could be consumed in addressing the question of adjudicated facts, and it would be time ill spent if in the end of the day the issues were simply reconsidered on the basis of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I understand the Court's position. And I saw that that matter was addressed to some extent or raised in the context of the 65 ter. And that seems to me to be a matter that is advanced by the type of discussion the Court has raised now, that is, what are the Prosecution's intentions with respect to the issues embraced by the 65 -- by the adjudicated facts submission and for the Prosecution for its part to know what the lay of the land might be should those matters be challenged. As I say, I certainly understand the Court's position. If everybody's putting -- and we've already put tremendous effort into the adjudicated facts motion with the expectation that it can have a positive effect on the expeditious nature of the trial. So that has been our intention. Obviously we have to consider the factors the court mentioned, but it seems to me there is a way through that thicket if there's proper communication, first of all beginning with the approach the Court just suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think that you should give this a thought prior to the next Status Conference because the first motion perhaps doesn't present so many problems, but the second one would because of its size. By the time of the next Status Conference, we may know what the response to that motion is, and we can then perhaps address this in a more informed way. So I think you should have in mind the possibility that the accused would be expected to challenge specifically and give reasons for challenging those facts which he does not accept insofar as they are set out specifically in the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I'd only add one additional matter, Your Honour, and that is, again having reviewed the 65 ter Conference transcript and seeing that this matter was raised and that the question was raised about other cases in which adjudicated facts had been presented, I went back and looked at some of those cases, and the adjudicated facts submissions and rulings have been on motions that were quite extensive and detailed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the trouble is that none of these cases have reached their conclusion yet, and therefore it remains to be seen how effective these early decisions were, much as they are to be commended.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I do understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you've heard that discussion about the Prosecution motions to have the Chamber take judicial notice of adjudicated facts. Is there anything on that subject that you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of facts that the Prosecution refer to in their first motion is an enormous one, but I have already responded. I'm going to respond to the other motion once I've received it; however, I have not received it. I wish to say, though, that I do not wish to assist the OTP in any way. I am going to challenge everything. I am going to adduce evidence. We can only agree perhaps on whether it was sunny on a particular day or rainy. Everything else is going to be challenged, starting with joint criminal enterprise and everything that happened on the ground. Everything is controversial. Everything is going to be challenged and the Prosecution should be aware of that. We are going to challenge everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are matters, though, which don't necessarily go to the root of the case against you, that -- but are important as background for a proper understanding of the events that occurred. And some of them may relate to dates, for example, of events which you don't dispute. Have you not considered whether there are elements in there that don't really require to be challenged?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the time being, I only have in mind the weather; that I'm not going to challenge, but we'll see how things evolve over time. If it's sunny, I'm not going to challenge that. I will agree that it was sunny, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, that exhausts the matters I have for consideration. Is there anything else you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No, there's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, is there anything else you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, yes. One of the most important questions is that in Bosnia-Herzegovina the OTP is carrying out certain actions that would have caused such an effect in your countries that perhaps this case would be dropped altogether. In addition to what happened on the 2nd of December, this is now the second time - and now we even have this on paper, we have tangible evidence, and we have persons who we can now recognise as working on behalf of the OTP - they are conducting searches, assaults, completely illegal actions against the homes of my immediate or extended family as they search for documents that are important for my case. This involves many different aspects. First of all, I am here now, and there is no reason whatsoever to disturb my family or my friends; secondly, I am in the process of collecting evidence. If somebody wishes to seize that evidence from my family or friends who are collecting this for me, that means an obstruction of my defence. I know that you said once that you wonder what the Trial Chamber has to do with that; however, now there is written evidence of what the Prosecution has been doing. This is yet another link in this endless chain of irregularities on behalf of the OTP. I ask the Chamber to order the OTP and the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina that they stop with all these searches for my evidence, to stop approaching my family and friends, and stop approaching my potential witnesses, even more so because these actions can actually be taken as intimidation of my potential witnesses. This is something that the Trial Chamber truly has to deal with because the Trial Chamber is in charge of the regularity of these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the written evidence that you say is available of -- to substantiate this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, those who carried out investigations left warrants that were given to them by the Office of the Prosecutor of Bosnia-Herzegovina working on orders from the Prosecutors here, collecting documents that will be used in the proceedings against me in this Tribunal. They were looking for this in the apartment of my sister-in-law this time, and the persons that are referred to as investigators are those who are immediately responsible to this OTP, and we know them from before.
