I cannot believe that they haven't got all the documents that they are looking for. They are looking for the archives of Republika Srpska. On the basis of what did they indict me if they don't have all those documents already? On the basis of what have I been indicted in the first place? This looks like nervous gunmen who first shoot and then ask questions. In my view, the Prosecution is totally unprepared, and I am footing the bill and the Defence. The regularity of these proceedings is being infringed upon. I really don't get nervous all that easily, but they are causing me pain by terrorising my family and my friends. Excellencies, hundreds of people there are jeopardised because of me. Leave aside my family. Hundreds of my friends to this day do not have personal documents, they don't have the right to travel, and now everyone has seen how I lived in Belgrade, and I really don't want to behave like a person from folklore of our people. I did not really have others supporting me. I lived on my own, and hundreds of people suffered a great deal because of me. To this day they have been denied all their rights. And in the meantime they continue searching for my potential documents and material -- documents and witnesses. That is impermissible. I think that the case would have been thrown out of court in many Western countries because of all these omissions and transgressions on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, what you have said does not contain any specific complaint of misconduct that we could have regard to or take any action in relation to. Indeed, you are not even directly the victim of any of the conduct that you describe. There are others, you say, that are affected. Well, it's a matter that they may choose to raise in the appropriate quarters. If you were to come into possession of any document indicating illegal conduct, then that's something you can draw to you are attention. If you have any other specific evidence of illegal conduct that you think we might have jurisdiction in relation to because it would interfere with the interests of justice here, then again that is something you can draw that to our attention. But in the absence of any specific complaint that would fall within our jurisdiction, there is no action we can take. Now, is there any other matter you wish to raise with us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have to clarify this. The OTP is instructing the authorities in -- of Bosnia-Herzegovina to search for evidence and documents that could be used against me in the homes of my family members. I am going to give you a copy of that search warrant and what it is that they're looking for. That is intimidation of my witnesses. That jeopardises my defence. It is a matter that this Trial Chamber is supposed to deal with. This is an attempt to seize what I may have collected so far as evidence. It doesn't have to do with my sister-in-law or my friends; it has to do with me. They are suffering, but I am suffering too. And also in the process my collection of evidence is being jeopardised. I kindly ask that you order that these persons and documents be protected. They do not have the right to barge into people's homes and collect documents that they may use against me. They cannot do this in this stage. I am here now. Now I have the right to collect evidence for my defence and to disclose this if I decide to do so. I can file a motion to have the case dismissed as such because my rights are being violated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The points that you make in a very general way do not on the face of it indicate illegal conduct. You say that you are in possession of a document. If you wish to invite the Chamber to take any action, you will have to submit a written motion indicating in what respect you consider that there is illegal conduct occurring that amounts to an interference with the interests of justice and invite us to take action on that. But from what you've said, it does not at first sight appear as if that test will be met; however, we'll leave it to you to decide whether to submit the matter with a written motion. Now, is there any other issue that you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to deal with it briefly, that is why I asked for it orally, to have this order issued to them, that they stop impeding my defence. However, it is with pleasure that I'm going to file this motion, explaining what it is that they are asking from my family. And I understand that in this way they are obstructing my defence; they are also disturbing the life of my family; and also they're trying to take away documents that may be used here in court by me and my defence. That is the most important matter that I wanted to deal with here and now in addition to all the other irregularities that threatened the possibility of a fair trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you for your submissions and your assistance. And thank you to the Prosecution also for their submissions and assistance. We anticipate that there should be another Status Conference roughly four weeks from now and tentatively indicate that that will be on the 6th of May. There will be a Scheduling Order in due course specifying the time and confirming the date. That brings this Status Conference to a conclusion. The court is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: adjourned at 5.50 p.m.
